anomalies.observed: Q1, the P-channel MOSFET controlled by the LTC4412, has its source on +5V and drain on USBC_VBUS_IN. U6 VIN is on USBC_VBUS_IN and SENSE is on +5V.
anomalies.expected: For the intended USB input-to-5V ideal-diode path, Q1 should have its source on USBC_VBUS_IN and drain on +5V, so the LTC4412 controls current from the USB input toward the board rail and blocks reverse current.

evidence.quote: USB power-path controller intended to OR/protect a USB power input

anomalies.impact: The MOSFET is oriented opposite to the intended ideal-diode power path. The USB input may only feed the rail through the body diode, while the controlled channel can permit incorrect or reverse current behavior, undermining USB power delivery and reverse-current protection.

anomalies.observed: SW6 is a two-pole DIP switch: one pole connects its pins 1–2 and the other connects pins 3–4 when closed. Its pin connections put CAN0_N through R34 to pin 1, CAN1_N through R35 to pin 2, CAN1_P on pin 3, and CAN0_P on pin 4. Closing the poles therefore cross-connects the two CAN channels, directly for the P lines and through the two resistors for the N lines.
anomalies.expected: The specification describes CAN0 and CAN1 as two isolated CAN buses. Their differential pairs should remain separate; any termination switching should connect a termination resistor across the P and N lines of its own bus, not bridge the two channels.
anomalies.impact: Closing the switch can couple the isolated CAN channels and disrupt differential signaling, potentially causing communication errors or bus faults.
